Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion, attaching the current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf) and our current subprocessor list (subprocessor_list.csv). A few follow-ups I promised to put in writing so your legal/infosec team can triage:

1) Controller vs. Processor: can you confirm whether Acme intends to be the Controller for customer user data and Redwood the Processor? On the call it sounded like Acme will be Controller for end-user data.

2) Subprocessors: attached list. Please flag any providers that require additional scrutiny.

3) Breach notice / timeline: you asked about our notification timeline for confirmed incidents. Our standard is notification within 72 hours for confirmed incidents affecting customer data; we have SOC2 processes for investigation.

4) Data residency & retention: default hosted logs/metrics are stored in the region where the tenant is provisioned (we can support EU-only residency for Dedicated/Private deployments). Default log retention is 90 days; we provide configurable retention options on Dedicated/Private. KV cache and ephemeral model context are not persisted beyond inference lifecycle unless configured by you.

5) PII handling: we don't train models on customer prompts. We provide options to disable retention of prompts/outputs for hosted customers upon contract and deployment configuration.

Next steps: if you can let me know which DPA sections you want edited or a marked redline, I'll loop in our legal and security folks (cc'ing them on follow-up). Also happy to set a quick call with your legal/infosec to walk through redlines.

Best,

Ben —

Thanks for the docs and the summary. A few clarifying questions from our side before we escalate to legal: 

- Controller/Processor: we expect Acme to be controller of end-user PII and Redwood to be processor. Please confirm this is the operating model covered by Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf.

- Subprocessors & notification: can you confirm whether Redwood provides a 30-day notice for new subprocessors and whether we can get an advance copy of the list before changes go live?

- Breach notice: 72 hours for confirmed incidents is fine; will Redwood provide a public incident report and root-cause summary to customers where applicable?

- Retention: default 90 days for logs is okay. We need confirmation that any request to persist prompts/outputs for fine-tuning will be opt-in and require our written approval.

- Data residency: for our EU customers we need to ensure all processing happens in EU regions — can you confirm EU-only processing is enforceable via contract for hosted accounts or if that requires a Dedicated/Private deployment?

If you can put the above into a short, written response we'll share with our legal/infosec and come back with redlines.

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below and proposed contractual language where useful. I've looped in Marissa (Legal) and Marcus (Security) to confirm implementation details.

- Controller/Processor: Confirmed — Acme Payment will be Controller and Redwood Inference will be Processor for customer-provided content. Proposed DPA sentence: "Customer is the Controller and Redwood Inference is the Processor with respect to Customer Data (as defined herein)." Marissa, please chime in if we should adjust.

- Subprocessors & notice: Our current policy is to provide 30 days' notice for the addition of material subprocessors and we publish an up-to-date subprocessor list (attached). For critical changes we will reach out directly to named contacts. We can include a clause to provide advance notice and a right to object within the DPA.

- Breach notice: We commit to notifying affected customers without undue delay and to provide initial notification within 72 hours of confirming a security incident affecting Customer Data. We will provide a follow-up root-cause summary and remediation steps as available.

- Retention & PII / model training: By default we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train models. Any retention of prompts/outputs for model improvements or fine-tuning is opt-in and requires Customer's explicit written consent. Ephemeral caches (KV caches) are not persisted beyond inference unless explicitly enabled by Customer; we can add explicit language to the DPA.

- Data residency: For Hosted customers we offer region-based provisioning; however, contractual EU-only processing for hosted tenants is limited and typically handled via our Dedicated/Private offering for guaranteed residency and contractual commitments. Marcus — can you confirm the technical limits and enforcement options we can contractually offer for hosted accounts?

Next steps: Marissa will provide a redline of the attached DPA with the proposed language for subprocessors, breach notifications, data residency notes, and retention. Happy to set a legal/infosec call — what times tomorrow look good for your team?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Sara —

I’m Marissa from Redwood Legal. Thanks for the questions — below are the concrete, redline-ready positions we can propose. I’ll attach a tracked-change DPA to this thread after internal sign-off.

1) Controller/Processor: We will include a clear clause: "Customer is Controller; Redwood is Processor." We’ll also add a short examples section describing customer content (prompts, end-user messages) as Customer Data.

2) Subprocessors: We’ll add a clause to: (a) maintain and publish the up-to-date subprocessor list, (b) provide 30 days' advance notice of material additions, and (c) provide a right to object. Exceptions for security/operational urgency will be narrowly tailored.

3) Breach notice: We agree 72-hour initial notification for confirmed incidents. We will commit to providing a follow-up incident report and remediation plan within a reasonable time frame (typically 30 days; emergency updates sooner).

4) Retention & training: We will add language that explicitly prohibits use of Customer Data for model training or improvements without Customer's prior written opt-in. Default log retention will be 90 days; Customers can request custom retention or Dedicated/Private deployment for longer retention controls.

5) Data residency: For guaranteed contractually-enforceable EU-only processing we will reference Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted accounts, we can commit to region-based provisioning but cannot guarantee contractual EU-only processing at parity with Dedicated/Private — we will call this out in the DPA.

Attachments to follow: redline DPA and current subprocessor list. If these positions look broadly acceptable, Ben can send over the DocuSign and we can iterate redlines. Happy to join a call if your legal/infosec wants to walk the redline live.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
